propositions: Two reliability test cases consume multi-second wall time due to production-scale timeouts and retry sleeps despite testing logical contracts rather than elapsed time.
The snapshot fetch stall abort test uses a 15-second real loopback server with a 10-second low-speed window when only one complete window cycle is semantically required.
The ACLI subprocess read-retry test uses a 1-second call timeout plus production backoff sleeps (2s/4s schedule) across three real child processes, totaling ~9 seconds of elapsed time.
Production defaults for timeout, stall, grace, drain, attempt, and backoff constants must remain unchanged while test-only injection points shrink the wall-clock execution time.
Every spawned PID must be confirmed absent after terminal failure using polling with a generous cleanup deadline, preserving process-group cleanup semantics.
